memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He slaughtered the ox and the ram as the fellowship offering for the people. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar." - Lev 9:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Last comes the fellowship offering — the offering of celebration, the one that ends in a shared meal.

Notice the sequence across this whole day. Sin dealt with. Life surrendered. Provision acknowledged. And now, finally, celebration.

God orders things so that joy comes last, not first. Not because joy is unimportant, but because joy built on unresolved sin is fragile. Celebration that skips the altar is only distraction.

Many people seek the feeling of closeness to God without the cost of dealing honestly with themselves. It never lasts. But the person who has genuinely brought their sin to God, surrendered their life, and given thanks — that person has something solid to celebrate.

James writes about this order: Come near to God and he will come near to you. Wash your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts... Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up (Jas 4:8-10). Humbling first, lifting afterward.

The joy of the LORD is your strength (Neh 8:10) — and it was said to people who had just wept over God's Word being read to them.

Deal with things honestly, and then celebrate freely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I seeking spiritual joy while avoiding honest dealing with sin?
2. Is there something unresolved that is stealing my ability to celebrate?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to deal honestly with what needs dealing with, so that my joy in You can be real. Amen.
